item.title: Usoro warns against fake news, deepfakes ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: FG honours Miden Systems chairman for business integrity By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has honoured the Executive Chairman of Miden Systems Limited, Dr Brendan Innocent Usoro, for corporate governance and business integrity, as he warned that fake news and artificial intelligence-generated misinformation posed growing threats to businesses, national security and Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. Usoro received the award at the Nigerian Press Council (NPC) National Summit on Curbing Fake News and Misinformation in the Nigerian Media Space, held in Abuja on Tuesday. The summit, organised under the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, brought together media practitioners, government officials, corporate executives, security agencies and other stakeholders to discuss ways of combating misinformation and promoting responsible journalism. Speaking at the event, Usoro said the growing use of artificial intelligence to generate fake audio recordings, manipulate videos and circulate fabricated reports had made it increasingly difficult for the public to distinguish facts from falsehoods. He said misinformation had extended beyond political campaigns to become a tool for damaging corporate reputations, undermining business confidence and creating social tension. “People use false information to de-market their political opponents, competitors’ products and services, as well as create tension in the polity,” he said. Usoro warned that deepfakes and coordinated disinformation campaigns could manipulate voters, erode public trust and undermine democratic institutions ahead of the 2027 elections. He also disclosed that Miden Systems had experienced what he described as the damaging effects of false information following a financial dispute with a commercial bank. To tackle the problem, he urged Nigerians to verify information before sharing it, recommending independent fact-checking platforms, including Dubawa, to establish the authenticity of reports, photographs and videos. He called for improved training for journalists and fact-checkers, as well as wider access to artificial intelligence-assisted verification tools. Usoro also urged technology companies and regulatory agencies, including the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) and the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), to strengthen collaboration in combating malicious synthetic media. He, however, cautioned that efforts to curb misinformation must not undermine press freedom, freedom of expression or legitimate criticism. On the company’s operations, Usoro said Miden Systems, established in 1997, had expanded from providing safety and equipment maintenance services into a diversified business covering marine services, logistics, offshore and onshore facility upgrades, maintenance and management. item.title: Dickson urges INEC to probe alleged AI-generated voter photos
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Seriake Dickson, has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to urgently investigate concerns over suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and questionable entries in the preliminary voter register published on its website. Dickson described the allegations as a serious matter requiring urgent attention, warning that failure to establish the facts and address any irregularities could undermine public confidence in the 2027 general elections. The former Bayelsa State governor spoke on Wednesday at his Abuja residence when he received the National Coordinator of the Dickson Movement for Democracy, Comrade Ogbidi Emmanuel, and other members of the group, who formally presented the organisation to him and decorated him as its Grand Patron. Dickson said INEC must provide a clear explanation of the allegations and take necessary steps to safeguard the integrity of the voter register. He acknowledged that the commission might have issued a response but maintained that it must go beyond statements to ensure the credibility of the database. “The issue of alleged AI-generated names and photographs in INEC’s voter register is a serious matter that deserves urgent attention. “It is not something that should be dismissed as mere speculation. Concerns have been raised about the authenticity of some entries, and INEC must address them promptly and transparently,” he said. The NDC leader said Nigerians were entitled to assurances that the approximately 103 million registered voters announced by the commission represented genuine and verifiable registrations by eligible citizens. He said the public needed confidence that the register did not contain fictitious identities, fabricated entries or photographs allegedly generated or manipulated using artificial intelligence. “We cannot afford to approach an election as consequential as the 2027 general election with a voter database whose integrity is in doubt,” he said. Dickson added that unreliable voter data could undermine the credibility of the electoral process, stressing the need for the commission to establish the facts surrounding the allegations. He warned that if investigations established that the register contained fictitious identities, photographs of deceased persons or images of individuals who were not eligible Nigerian voters, the development could damage INEC’s credibility and Nigeria’s international standing. He, however, noted that there was still time before the elections for the commission to address the concerns. “I therefore join other concerned Nigerians in calling on INEC to provide a clear explanation, establish the facts and take all necessary measures to clean up the register,” he said. Dickson urged Nigerians to take advantage of the statutory display of the voter register at designated locations to scrutinise entries and report suspicious or inaccurate information

item.title: Osun IPAC disowns members on Adeleke’s PCC list
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) in Osun State has disowned individuals listed as representatives of political parties in the Osun Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) by Governor Ademola Adeleke, the state coordinator of President Bola Tinubu’s campaign council. In a statement issued on Tuesday and endorsed by 11 political parties, Osun IPAC said the individuals listed as its representatives were acting on their own and had not been authorised to represent the council. The parties include Action Alliance, National Rescue Movement, Action Democratic Party, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Social Democratic Party and National Democratic Party. Others are Democratic Leadership Alliance, African Action Congress, Labour Party, Zenith Labour Party and All Progressives Grand Alliance. An advertorial signed by Adeleke and published in a national newspaper had listed Odeleye Titus, Faribido Benson, Enorch Olalekan, Adetunji Olubunmi, Prince Adesoji Adeleke and Rev. Olatunji Popoola as IPAC representatives in the Osun PCC. However, the council said the inclusion of their names was misleading and could create confusion over its representation. “We wish to state categorically and for the record, that the persons whose names were paraded as IPAC members in the said council are not our representatives, nor were they, at any point in time, nominated or authorised by the council to represent us in any capacity,” the statement said. IPAC described itself as a structured body with recognised leadership and member political parties, insisting that any representation must follow due process and official communication from its secretariat. The council said it completely dissociated itself from the list, warning against using its name to score political points or create a false impression of broad-based acceptance. It also urged President Tinubu not to recognise the individuals listed as its representatives in the Osun PCC, insisting that its legitimate stakeholders were parties with strong grassroots presence across the state’s local government areas. “We are the majority members of IPAC in Osun State with strong grassroots presence across all local governments, and any engagement with IPAC in the state should be through us,” the statement added. item.title: Oborevwori signs five bills into law in Delta
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi and Ochuko Akuopha ASABA — Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has signed five bills into law, saying the measures are aimed at strengthening public institutions, improving service delivery and securing a better future for residents. Oborevwori assented to the bills at Government House, Asaba, on Wednesday, describing them as part of his administration’s reform efforts under the MORE Agenda. “I assented to five bills, three amendments, one consolidated, and a brand-new one passed by the Delta State House of Assembly,” the governor said. The new laws are the Delta State Revenue Service (Consolidated) Law, 2026; Delta State Public and Private Properties Protection (Amendment) Law, 2026; High Court (Amendment) Law, 2026; Customary Court of Appeal (Amendment) Law, 2026; and Payment of Thirteenth Month Salary Law, 2026. Oborevwori said the laws would strengthen accountability, protect public assets, reinforce the rule of law and improve workers’ morale. “Together, we have strengthened accountability, safeguarded public assets, reinforced the rule of law and boosted public servants’ morale,” he said. He added that the measures reflected his administration’s determination to build institutions that serve residents with fairness, efficiency and respect. “These efforts reflect our resolve to build institutions that serve our people with fairness, efficiency and respect, while securing a better future for our people,” he said. The governor stressed that development went beyond infrastructure to include policies capable of improving people’s lives. On the Thirteenth Month Salary Law, Oborevwori said the initiative was intended to boost workers’ morale, reward their contributions and improve productivity. He also said the amendments to the laws governing the judiciary would increase the number of High Court judges from 46 to 50 and Customary Court of Appeal judges from nine to 12, with a view to improving justice delivery. According to him, the laws would strengthen public institutions, improve service delivery and promote economic development. Presenting the bills, Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Emomotimi Guwor, said the measures would strengthen governance, improve justice delivery and protect investments. item.title: Reps summon navy, police, customs over recovered assets
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has summoned the Nigerian Navy, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Customs Service, Nigeria Immigration Service and the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) over the management of seized, forfeited and recovered assets. The five agencies are expected to appear before a sub-committee investigating the management of such assets on November 2, 2026, as lawmakers seek to audit recovered assets, establish a unified digital registry and strengthen accountability. Chairman of the sub-committee, Hon. Ibe Okwara Osonwa, announced the date during the panel’s inaugural meeting in Abuja, following a motion moved by Hon. Omosede Igbinedion and seconded by other members. Osonwa, who represents Arochukwu/Ohafia Federal Constituency of Abia State, described the assignment as an important national responsibility, noting that the management, disposal and utilisation of recovered assets had continued to attract public concern and institutional scrutiny under successive administrations. He said questions had persisted over transparency, coordination and the integrity of processes governing assets seized or forfeited through anti-corruption investigations, criminal justice proceedings and administrative enforcement. “Across various administrations, questions have persisted regarding transparency, coordination, and the integrity of processes governing assets seized or forfeited through anti-corruption efforts, criminal justice actions, and administrative enforcement,” he said. According to the lawmaker, the concerns extended beyond administrative procedures, with implications for public trust, institutional credibility and the effectiveness of Nigeria’s anti-corruption framework. “These concerns are not merely technical—they strike at the heart of public trust, institutional credibility, and the effectiveness of Nigeria’s anti-corruption architecture,” Osonwa added. He explained that the sub-committee had been mandated to conduct a comprehensive audit to establish a clear and verifiable record of all seized, forfeited and recovered assets held or managed by relevant government agencies. The exercise would also seek to establish a unified digital registry capable of providing real-time information on recovered assets, preventing duplication of records and improving coordination among agencies involved in their recovery and management. Osonwa said the committee would further examine existing accountability mechanisms and recommend reforms in line with relevant laws and international best practices. “The sub-committee has the opportunity to recommend reforms that will close long-standing loopholes, modernise asset management systems, and reinforce Nigeria’s commitment to transparency and responsible stewardship,” he said. item.title: INEC verifies 5,277 functional BVAS machines in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has confirmed that 5,277 of the 5,381 Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines physically verified in Benue State are functional ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in the state, Aminu Idris, disclosed this on Wednesday at a stakeholders’ meeting at the INEC Benue State Collation Centre in Makurdi. Idris said the commission was taking necessary measures to ensure adequate deployment of functional BVAS devices for the elections. He also disclosed that Benue had 3,057,225 registered voters across its 23 local government areas, 276 registration areas and 5,102 polling units. The REC urged political parties, civil society organisations and the media to support efforts to ensure peaceful, free, fair, credible and inclusive elections in the state. “This stakeholders’ meeting provides us the opportunity to update critical stakeholders on the commission’s preparations for the 2027 general election,” he said. Idris said the presidential and National Assembly elections were scheduled for Saturday, January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections would hold on Saturday, February 6, 2027. He said all stakeholders had important roles to play in creating a peaceful environment for the conduct of credible elections. Giving an update on INEC’s preparations, the REC said the commission had commenced the delivery of non-sensitive election materials and other logistical assets to its state and area council offices. He added that the Benue State office had completed its BVAS inventory and status report in line with directives from the commission’s headquarters. “The ICT department has reported that out of the 5,381 BVAS devices physically verified, 5,277, representing 98 per cent, were found to be functional and ready for deployment,” he said. According to Idris, the commission’s headquarters had been notified of the number of devices that were faulty or damaged beyond repair, while measures were being taken to ensure the state had the required number of functional machines for the elections. INEC receives 1,052 voter register claims, objections The REC also disclosed that INEC had concluded the Registration Area-level display of the voter register for claims and objections across the state’s 23 local government areas between October 9 and 15, 2026. He said the exercise generated 1,052 claims and objections, comprising 947 claims and 105 objections. Idris added that the commission made Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) available for collection during the period by voters who had yet to collect their cards and those whose cards were processed during Phase One of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise, conducted between August 25 and December 10, 2025. item.title: Shinkafi to INEC: Withdraw Yau’s name as APC senatorial candidate in Zamfara
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Following the Court of Appeal judgment upholding the nullification of the APC primary in Zamfara North Senatorial District, party chieftain and aspirant, Dr Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to withdraw Senator Sahabi Alhaji Ya’u’s name as the party’s candidate. Shinkafi accused INEC of disregarding subsisting court judgments by continuing to publish Ya’u’s name, insisting that the commission must respect the ruling and allow a fresh primary involving all cleared aspirants. In a statement, Shinkafi said his lawyer had written to the INEC chairman, demanding the withdrawal. The letter, dated October 27, 2026, was signed by S.Y. Aliyu of Yas Law Firm. The Court of Appeal, Sokoto Division, on October 20 dismissed Ya’u’s appeal as grossly unmeritorious and affirmed the Federal High Court, Gusau judgment nullifying the disputed primary and ordering a fresh exercise. “It is curious that INEC continues to parade Senator Sahabi Alhaji Ya’u as the APC Zamfara North Senatorial candidate in defiance of the Court of Appeal judgment and the Federal High Court Gusau judgment,” Shinkafi said. His lawyer urged INEC to withdraw Ya’u’s name pending a fresh primary or the final determination of the dispute by the Supreme Court. Shinkafi alleged that unnamed anti-democratic forces were working to prevent the APC from fielding a candidate in the district, warning that the dispute could jeopardise the party’s participation in the 2027 general elections. “Let it be clear, this injustice shall not stand,” he said. item.title: Reps threaten arrest warrants for telecom CEOs
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has threatened to issue arrest warrants against chief executives of telecommunications companies over their failure to honour invitations to explain persistent poor network services across the country. The warning followed the rejection on Wednesday by the House Ad Hoc Committee investigating telecommunications service quality of an attempt by the Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria (ALTON) to represent the affected companies through its chairman, Engr. Gbenga Adebayo. The committee, chaired by Rep. Olumide Osoba (APC, Ogun), directed the chief executives and top management officials of MTN Nigeria, Airtel Nigeria, Globacom, Mafab Communications and other affected operators to appear before it on November 4, 2026, or risk arrest warrants. The lawmakers expressed displeasure with the operators’ decision to delegate Adebayo to represent them, insisting that each company must personally account for its service delivery and address complaints from millions of subscribers. The committee had initially invited the operators on October 21 to explain persistent complaints of dropped calls, slow internet connectivity, failed airtime and data transactions, and inadequate network coverage. Moving a motion on the matter, Rep. Sunday Umeha argued that the telecommunications companies were individually licensed by the Federal Government and could not rely on their membership of an industry association to avoid direct accountability before the legislature. He also faulted a letter reportedly written by ALTON questioning the committee’s authority to compel the operators to appear, describing the association’s position as inconsistent with the constitutional responsibilities of the National Assembly. “I was shocked with what I saw in the letter. I saw a situation where ALTON is saying that they are not bound to appear before this committee. They see their appearance as a privilege to this committee and not as a statutory obligation,” Umeha said. Citing Section 88 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the lawmaker maintained that the National Assembly had the authority to investigate matters within its legislative competence, including the implementation of government policies affecting telecommunications services. He insisted that the committee was not bound by ALTON’s internal arrangements and that the operators must appear individually unless the lawmakers expressly accepted an authorised representative. A representative of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) reinforced the committee’s position, confirming that the commission had communicated the invitations directly to the chief executives of the affected companies. The confirmation further angered the lawmakers, who said the operators had received adequate notice and sufficient opportunities to honour the invitations. item.title: Alake denies $700bn minerals sale, inaugurates Nigeria-US committee
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, has dismissed reports that Nigeria sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to the United States, insisting that no national asset has been sold or transferred under the bilateral cooperation framework. Alake spoke on Tuesday in Abuja while inaugurating the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector, describing the reports as false and clarifying that the agreement was designed to attract investment and promote partnerships between American investors and Nigerian operators. “There is no sale of any Nigerian asset. There’s nothing exchanging hands,” he said. The minister explained that the memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by Nigeria and the US was a government-to-government platform intended to facilitate business-to-business engagements, rather than transfer ownership of Nigeria’s mineral resources to foreign interests. “We created a platform to facilitate mingling of US investment ventures with Nigeria’s local operators. It is in the public domain. We signed it in public and published it in four or five national newspapers,” he said. The committee’s inauguration followed the strategic cooperation framework established between both countries during the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York. Alake also dismissed claims that the United States intended to take over Nigeria’s mineral resources and security architecture, describing the reports as misleading. He said the partnership aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s economic diversification agenda, which seeks to reduce the country’s dependence on crude oil through the sustainable development of its mineral resources. According to him, Nigeria is seeking to change the pattern of international economic transactions in which resource-rich African countries export raw materials without retaining sufficient value from their exploitation. “We have the resources, the critical elements the world needs to transit to clean energy. So we are creating a new paradigm — you bring your capital, expertise and technology, to match with our natural resources and create a win-win situation. The investor gains, Nigeria gains,” he said. The minister lamented that Nigeria had historically operated a mono-product economy, while much of its solid minerals sector remained informal, with ores transported “from pit to port” without adequate local processing. He said the Federal Government had introduced a policy making local processing a condition for the granting of mineral titles, adding that investors must demonstrate a clear pathway for processing minerals within the country. item.title: Alleged $2.1m land deal: Lawyers bicker over case against Wike’s son
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — Two senior lawyers have engaged in a war of words over the ongoing case concerning an alleged $2.1m Abuja land transaction involving Jordan Nyesom-Wike, son of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Jordan’s lawyer, Dr. Ogwu Onoja, SAN, accused Ibrahim Waru, counsel to the claimants, of distorting the facts of the case with lies which, he said, were aimed at tarnishing the reputation of his client, who, he said, openly denied any involvement in the alleged land racket during his court appearance. He insisted that his client neither had any transaction with the claimants nor admitted collecting the money. “This haze of lies and malicious fabrication appears to be an orchestrated media campaign intended to whip up sentiments, compromise the mind of the public and intimidate the judge. “For the record, Jordan Wike, in his defence before the court, stated in unequivocal terms that he has never met Safwan Garba G.Y. or any of his agents at any time. “He maintained this line of defence while giving evidence in court on 28 and 30 September 2026. One therefore wonders why a lawyer would grant interviews to misrepresent what transpired in court weeks after the proceedings. “It is baffling that this interview by I.G. Waru was granted this week at the Federal High Court, Abuja, close to a month after the proceedings at the FCT High Court. It is clearly the source of defamatory comments, unfounded claims and unproven conclusions being made on social media by ignorant members of the public,” Onoja, SAN, added in a statement he made available to journalists. However, reacting to the statement on Wednesday, Waru insisted that his clients are in possession of the signature of Wike’s son on the acknowledgement receipt for the $2.1m paid for the disputed land. In the statement titled “Re-joinder on the Press Statement Signed by Dr. Ogwu J. Onoja, SAN, FCArb, Lead Counsel to Jordan Nyesom-Wike in Respect of the $2.1 Million Matter,” Waru stood by his claim. The rejoinder read in part: “Having perused the statement signed by Dr. Onoja, SAN, for and on behalf of Jordan Nyesom-Wike, we found it necessary to respond, thus: “All that was stated during the interview granted by I.G. Waru Esq. was drawn from the hard record of proceedings and processes issued in suit No. FCT/HC/CV/008/2026, just like the signature of Jordan Wike on the acknowledgement receipt of the sum of $2.1m that he received from Safwan Garba GY on the 17th October, 2025. “The signature contained therein is the same as the one signed by Jordan Wike on his witness statement on oath before the court and, most importantly, the same as the specimen signature obtained from him in the witness box, after he was given a pen and paper and asked to sign five times. “Being a public document, it can be obtained by any member of the general public who, by virtue of Section 104(1) of the Evidence Act, applies for a copy.” Waru said the interview was granted to sensitise me

item.title: Fubara warns Rivers traditional rulers against partisan politics
item.description: By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has urged traditional rulers in the state to remain neutral in partisan politics, promote fairness and preserve peace in their communities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Fubara gave the charge on Wednesday while declaring open the 126th, 127th and 128th combined quarterly meeting of the Rivers State Traditional Rulers Council in Port Harcourt. He reminded the royal fathers that their primary responsibility was to administer justice, ensure fairness and promote peaceful coexistence, warning that their conduct should not create divisions or crises that could be difficult to manage. “As we are entering into this political season actively, everyone should ensure that your conduct promotes peace in your place. Your actions should not be what would lead to the division and multiple crises that we cannot manage as a government,” the governor said. He urged the traditional rulers to uphold the oaths and constitutional provisions they subscribed to before ascending their respective stools, stressing the need to protect the stability and progress of Rivers State. Fubara also called on them to set aside personal sentiments and place the interests of the state above individual considerations. “I want to enjoin everyone to keep aside issues of individual sentiments and ensure that the interest of our state supersedes whatever thing that we have in our mind,” he said. The governor added that prioritising the state’s interests was a principle he said had guided his day-to-day administration. On the welfare concerns raised by the traditional rulers, Fubara said delays in addressing some of their previous requests were not attributable to the state government but to the council’s inability to put its house in order. He explained that stipends paid to traditional rulers by local government councils were statutory benefits and not matters a governor could alter through verbal pronouncements. The governor, however, assured the royal fathers that he would fulfil his promises to them before leaving office next year. Fubara reaffirmed his respect for the traditional institution, describing its members as custodians of culture and tradition and an important link between government and the grassroots. He thanked the rulers for their prayers and support, urging them to ensure that the meeting produced fruitful deliberations capable of strengthening peace and development in the state. Earlier, the Chairman of the Rivers State Council of Traditional Rulers and Paramount Ruler of Apara Kingdom, Eze Chike Amadi Worlu Wodo, thanked the state government for maintaining a cordial relationship with the traditional institution. Wodo highlighted the role of traditional rulers in conflict resolution, noting that their proximity to residents placed them in a strategic position to mediate disputes involving chieftaincy matters, families and land ownership. item.title: Police arrest two over alleged kidnap plot in Kano
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has arrested two 20-year-old men over an alleged plot to kidnap the village head of Bangare in Gezawa Local Government Area of the state. The suspects, identified as Aliyu Naziru Garba and Bashir Alhasan, were arrested following a report that the traditional leader, Mallam Idris, had received threats of abduction. The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Wednesday. Kiyawa said Idris reported the threat at the Gezawa Divisional Police Headquarters at about 1:30 a.m. on October 26, stating that an unidentified person had called him two days earlier and threatened to kidnap him. “Following the report, police operatives attached to the Gezawa Division launched an operation which led to the arrest of the two suspects,” he said. Kiyawa added that the suspects had confessed to the crime, while investigations were ongoing. He said they would be charged to court upon the conclusion of the investigation. The Commissioner of Police in Kano State, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the officers for their swift response and professional handling of the case. Bakori reiterated the command’s commitment to tackling criminal activities across the state. The police urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious persons or movements to the nearest police station. item.title: Ebonyi opposition protests proposed ₦150m billboard fee
item.description: By Anayo Okoli Opposition parties and residents of Ebonyi State have criticised a proposed ₦150 million fee for political campaign billboards, describing the measure as excessive and warning that it could restrict political competition ahead of the 2027 elections. The controversy followed a motion by the Deputy Chief Whip of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly, Hon. Arinze Lucas Chukwu, seeking to address what he described as the indiscriminate pasting of political posters and erection of billboards in the state capital. Opposition figures, however, argued that the proposed fee could make it difficult for parties and candidates outside the ruling party to publicise their campaigns. The governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in the 2027 election, Dr. Kingsley Agbor, described the proposal as “unfortunate and devastating”. Agbor accused the administration of Governor Francis Nwifuru of attempting to restrict the political space for opposition parties. He said the proposed fee could undermine democratic participation and recalled the sacrifices made by Nigerians in the struggle to end military rule. “The government of Nwifuru once again wants to stifle the political space for the opposition political parties to operate. This is seen with this outrageous cost of elections and campaign billboards,” he said. Agbor alleged that the proposal reflected a desire to establish a one-party state, adding that opposition parties should not be silenced in a democracy. The governorship candidate of the Labour Party, Chief Splendour Oko-Eze, also condemned the proposal, describing it as an attempt to restrict opposition activities in the state. In an open letter, Oko-Eze questioned how opposition candidates would raise ₦150 million merely to erect campaign billboards and display posters. “Opposition is not a crime anywhere in the world. It is the beauty of democracy. It acts like a watchdog to the government in power so as to make sure that the dividends of democracy get to the people,” he said. He argued that the performance of an incumbent administration, rather than restrictions on opposition campaigns, should determine whether voters return it to office. Oko-Eze also questioned whether the proposed measure would apply equally to campaign billboards belonging to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). “How much did Governor Chief Francis Ogbonnaya Nwifuru and wife pay for all their billboards scattered all over the state? Or does it mean the law is just made for opposition parties and their candidates?” he asked. He urged lawmakers to ensure that legislation served the interests of residents rather than intimidate political parties and candidates. item.title: Senate seeks institution named after Fasoranti
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has called on the Federal Government to immortalise the late elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, by naming an educational institution after him in recognition of his contributions to education and national development. The Senate made the call on Wednesday while mourning Fasoranti, who died on October 20, 2026, at the age of 100. The lawmakers observed a minute’s silence in his honour and resolved to send a delegation to convey the Senate’s condolences to his family and the people of Ondo State. The resolutions followed the consideration of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Senator Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central), titled, “The Demise of Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, the Foremost Leader of Pan-Yoruba Socio-Political Organisation, Afenifere, and a Revered Political Leader from Akure, Ondo State.” Presenting the motion, Adegbonmire said Fasoranti left behind a legacy of service to humanity and significant contributions to Nigeria. Born on May 11, 1926, in Akure, Ondo State, Fasoranti had a professional background in education, which, according to the senator, influenced his approach to governance and commitment to human welfare. Adegbonmire noted that the late elder statesman established Omolere Nursery and Primary School and Akure High School, among other educational institutions, contributing to the development of education in Ondo State. He said Fasoranti emerged as leader of Afenifere after the death of Pa Abraham Adesanya. The senator also recalled that Fasoranti was a committed follower of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo, leader of the Action Group during the First Republic, and later associated with the Unity Party of Nigeria during the Second Republic. He was also a founding member of the Alliance for Democracy. Fasoranti served as commissioner for finance in the old Ondo State under the administration of the late Governor Michael Adekunle Ajasin between 1979 and 1985. Adegbonmire described him as a respected elder statesman whose life was defined by service, integrity and commitment to the Yoruba people and Nigeria. He said Fasoranti was among prominent Nigerians who opposed military rule and advocated the restoration of democratic governance. The senator added that the deceased remained steadfast in the struggle for democracy, spoke truth to power and promoted collaboration among socio-political groups, including Arewa and Ohanaeze Ndigbo, in pursuit of a united and prosperous Nigeria. He said Fasoranti’s death marked the end of a remarkable era, but his legacy of principled leadership, wisdom and dedication to national progress would continue to inspire future generations. Adegbonmire also prayed for the repose of the deceased’s soul and strength for his family, the Afenifere organisation, Ondo State and the country to bear the loss. item.title: [UPDATED] High-Speed Train Collision In Spain Kills 64, Injures Over 100
item.description: A high-speed train collision south of Madrid in Spain killed 64 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said in one of Europe’s deadliest such disasters this century. One train on the scene in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha was seen embedded into another after the second such accident to strike Spain this year. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Civil Guard on October 28, 2026 shows an aerial scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. (Photo by Handout / Guardia Civil / AFP) Some carriages were lying on their side in tangles of metal debris at the bottom of an embankment, while dozens of emergency services vehicles were racing to and from the site. “We are speaking of approximately 64 (dead), but this is probably going to grow even more,” Castilla-La Mancha’s leader Emiliano Garcia-Page told reporters at the scene, raising a previous toll of 31. A spokeswoman from the Castilla-La Mancha government said that more than 100 people had been injured. Of them, 58 had been taken to hospital, with 15 in a critical condition. Helicopters hovered above the site during a frantic search for survivors, while several black vans arrived from a funeral parlour. State railway operator Renfe confirmed in a statement that the main high-speed line from Madrid to southern Spain had been suspended after one of its services suffered an accident with a train from private Spanish company Iryo. Iryo said in a statement that its train, which was carrying 147 passengers and five staff, including the driver, “was hit from behind” by the Renfe service. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Emergency Military Unit (UME) on October 28, 2026 shows military rescue personnel working at the scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. Photo by HANDOUT / UME / AFP A visibly shaken Manuel Ortiz, 49, who lives in the nearby village of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid, told AFP he had been transporting survivors all morning in his car. Ortiz added that the passengers of the Iryo told him their train was stationary when the collision happened, describing a “horrific, horrible” scene that “smelled of an accident, of metal”. Rail Safety Under Scrutiny The accident comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faced heavy criticism for this year’s first disaster, seeks to overturn unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership in an early general election on November 29. Sanchez’s office said he was heading to the scene. The premier had said on X that he was “shocked” by the accident and sent “my love, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families”.
